newsitem.title: FRANCE: Palestinian, Israeli share French rights prizes.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian, Israeli share French rights prizes.

text.p: France on Tuesday awarded joint human rights prizes to the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights and the Public Committee against Torture in Israel, with another award going to the dissident Cuban Human Rights Commission.

In a symbolic gesture highlighting his appeals for peace in the Middle East, President Jacques Chirac handed out the awards at his Elysee palace, sharing a 100,000-franc ($20,000) prize between Israel's Lea Tsemel and Palestinian Raji Surani.

"Granting the award to both groups was a very special and unique gesture of support," Surani later told a joint news conference with Tsemel, who was Surani's lawyer when he was in detention in Israel.
Chirac recently toured the Middle East, visiting both Arab countries and Israel and chiding overzealous Israeli police on a tour of Arab east Jerusalem.

Tsemel was singled out for opposing the use of torture during the questioning of detainees. Surani received the award for his Gaza-based group's programme to prepare Palestinian society for democracy.

Cuban Elizardo Sanchez received a 100,000-franc ($20,000) prize for the legal and humanitarian assistance his Committee for Human Rights and National Reconciliation gives dissidents seeking democracy on the Communist-ruled Caribbean island.

President Fidel Castro's government has frequently acted against dissidents it has accused of being part of U.S. efforts to destroy Cuba's one-party system. Dissidents have been jailed for offences like rebellion, enemy propaganda or holding illegal meetings.

Other awards went to the Helsinki Human Rights Committee for monitoring rights in Bosnia, Colombia's Jose Alvear Restrepo lawyers group for working to improve prison conditions, and Roman Catholic priests in Madagascar for helping destitute detainees.
